subject: Post-call: TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Mary Li <mary.li@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T15:10:00Z
Subject: Post-call: TCO recap & next steps

John / Mary —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned and we have clear next steps. High-level notes from the call: 

Pain points we heard
- Token cost is the single biggest blocker for your pilot economics (you quoted a hard cap of ~$25k/mo for inference).
- Spiky traffic (batch marketing bursts) causing unpredictable spend and some latency SLO misses.
- Need to preserve response quality for customer-facing prompts; internal analytics can tolerate lower fidelity.
- Compliance: data residency requirements for EU users and audit logs for billing reconciliation.

Goals / success criteria
- Keep inference spend under $25k/month for pilot while serving 2–3M queries/mo (avg 150–200 tokens per request).
- 95th percentile latency < 250ms for customer-facing flows.
- Demo/POC with engineering within the next 2 weeks.

Cost levers we discussed (how Redwood can help)
- Batching & concurrency tuning: continuous batching to improve GPU utilization for peak bursts (expect ~15–30% token-cost reduction for synchronous flows).
- Prefix/KV caching: cache repeated prefixes and conversational state for logged-in users — can reduce generation tokens by 20–50% depending on reuse.
- Model routing: route lower-risk internal queries to a smaller, cheaper variant; route critical customer prompts to the higher-quality model.
- Quantization & Dedicated profiles: 8-bit quantization + dedicated pools to lower per-token inference costs and stabilize latency.
- Autoscaled Dedicated capacity + smart routing to avoid expensive on-demand egress during spikes.

Initial TCO sketch (high level)
- Baseline (current): rough estimate per your numbers = ~1B tokens/mo => ~$18k–27k/mo (depends on model mix).
- With batching + caching + model routing + quantization: projected reduction 45–60% => target $8k–12k/mo for equivalent throughput.

Next steps
1) I attached a short TCO worksheet (redwood_tco_estimate_acme_v1.xlsx) with a model-by-model breakdown and assumptions — please review and I can tailor numbers to your exact traffic profile.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/ML team (suggested: Aug 6 or 7) — engineering deep-dive to validate latency SLOs and network/region constraints.
3) If the numbers look good, we can spin up a 2-week POC on Dedicated capacity with an evaluated cap and telemetry for cost and quality.

Please tell me if I missed anything or if you want different slices in the TCO sheet (e.g., 99th pct latency or per-route breakdown).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and aligned to what we discussed. A few quick clarifications before we dig into the spreadsheet:

- Our prod traffic estimate for the pilot is closer to 2.5M queries/mo (we'd previously given 3M as a high-water). Average token usage should be ~175 tokens per request (post-editing).
- For caching: most reuse is in the 30–40% range for the knowledge-base responses, but customer prompts are unique.
- We absolutely need EU residency for EU customers; US-hosted for NA is fine.

Can you highlight in the workbook a line showing the "pilot cap" at $25k/mo with what that buys (QPS, model mix, latency)? Also cc our procurement contact if we move toward an NDA/POC.

John —

Thanks for the quick notes. I updated the attached workbook to include a "pilot cap" tab that shows:
- What $25k/mo buys (approx throughput, model mix split, expected 95th pct latency)
- Two scenarios: conservative reuse (30% caching) and optimistic reuse (50% caching)
- Suggested Dedicated config to keep latency consistent during bursts (2-node pool + burst to on-demand).

Top-line for your numbers (2.5M queries/mo, 175 tokens avg):
- Baseline (hosted, no cache, high-quality model for all): ~$21k/mo
- With caching (~35%), batching, and routing (mix of high-quality + cheaper variant): ~$11.5k/mo
- With added quantization on cheaper variant and Dedicated pool: ~$9k/mo

I've called out the primary assumptions in the workbook (sheet: assumptions) — if you can confirm QPS shape (hourly distribution) and the percent of customer-facing vs internal queries, I can tighten the estimate.

Suggested next meetings:
- Technical deep-dive (eng + infra) — Aug 6, 10:00am PT (I'll send a calendar invite).
- Procurement intro (procurement + solutions engineer) — Aug 9 if you prefer.

Marissa
